finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards the boolean return value. requireRole never throws, so the OWNER check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can wipe any tenant. The sibling export() uses checkRole(), which throws, and is enforced.
finding.source: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe: authenticated caller-supplied User (any roles) and the tenant path parameter
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 (destructive wipe of tenant data)

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler entry. It receives the user and the tenant from the path.
requireRole only returns u.roles().contains(role). Its javadoc says it does not throw.
The returned boolean is ignored, so there is no abort or throw when the user lacks OWNER.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is requireRole at line 26, and its result is unused, so it does nothing. The sibling export() at line 32 uses checkRole, which throws SecurityException, so export is SAFE with respect to the role check. Neither handler compares the tenant to the user's own tenant. User has no tenant field, so an OWNER of one tenant could also act on another. I could not see the caller-side tenant scoping because only this file exists.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:26 returns a boolean and never throws (lines 13-16); the result is discarded. No other guard exists in this file. checkRole (lines 18-22) throws but is only used in export().
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls the non-throwing requireRole (14-16) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated user, whereas export() at line 32 correctly uses the throwing checkRole.
